messages.subject: Enserco — exposure run review, Apr 17–19
messages.body:
Following up on the limit-breach question you raised this morning.

Pulled the daily exposure workbooks Person C runs for Enserco. The Apr 17 close shows $4.2M net of L/C collateral — clean, inside the $5M ceiling. The Apr 18 close is $5.3M net. That's the crossing point; the limit was gone by end of day Apr 18.

What the workbook entry says for Apr 18 is 'approaching limit / collateral review pending.' That language doesn't reflect what the number actually shows.

More to the point: the ticket log for Apr 18 afternoon and Apr 19 shows at least three trades booked after the $5.3M figure was on the screen. Person C processed that batch — her initials are on the clearance queue for each one. So the trades that pushed through after the line crossed weren't a system gap; they went through the normal workflow.

I'd want to know when the over-limit alert was supposed to go out and why it didn't, but that's a separate thread. For now the exposure picture is: counterparty is over its approved ceiling, has been since Apr 18 close, and additional volume was booked on top of that.

Let me know how you want to handle escalation.

The bigger issue is the unsigned ISDA, which Person B is chasing. Once that's executed we can revisit the limit itself if the desk wants to grow the relationship.

Person B, looping you in so you know the desk has been told to pause. Let me know if you need anything else from my end on the ISDA chase.

messages.subject: Re: Clearwater Valley — opinion letter status
messages.body:
Person C —

Following up on your call from last month. To confirm what I told you then: under the plain language of the PUC order, the conditional authorization to trade financial derivatives requires a current opinion letter from outside counsel. The August 1998 letter was a one-year instrument. Without a successor letter in place, the authorization is lapsed as of August 1999 — it's not a gray area.

I understand you sent a renewal request to Clearwater Valley's counsel on September 15th. If no response has come back by now, there's nothing for me to work with on my end. The authorization doesn't carry over on the strength of the request alone.

Let me know if you need anything in writing beyond this, but I'd want to flag that any trades running against this counterparty in the interim are running without a valid regulatory authorization in place.

— J

Person J | Local Regulatory Counsel
Direct: 208-555-0174

messages.subject: Re: counterparty delivery failures — file status
messages.body:
B —

For your awareness, since this is now coming up with the desk: the FM checklist on the counterparty notice came back clean a few days ago. Event was foreseeable, within their operational control, and the notice landed outside the contractual window — all three grounds for rejection were met. F drafted the rejection letter, it went out to the counterparty, and the file was closed on the FM question. That letter is in the outgoing correspondence log under F's contract file.

Counterparty has been in active breach of its delivery obligations since the rejection issued. The missed deliveries since then are not suspensions under a live FM claim — the claim is gone.

Not sure what's holding up the breach declaration on the desk side, but from a contract-status standpoint there's nothing open on FM. Flagging in case it's useful for whatever is being worked through upstairs.

C

messages.subject: Re: counterparty — FM review / desk query
messages.body:
G —

Following up on our call. To put it in writing so you have something to work from:

We haven't issued a final determination on the FM claim yet. There are concerns about whether the notice meets the contractual standard, but that review isn't closed. My strong recommendation is that we tell the desk to hold off on any formal breach declaration until we complete the assessment — a few more days at most.

Reason: if we issue a default notice while the FM claim is technically still live and a court later finds the claim valid, we're exposed to a wrongful-termination argument. That's a worse position than a short delay. Getting the FM question fully buttoned up first is the cleaner path and protects us if this ends up in dispute.

Happy to discuss further, but I wouldn't want the desk moving on a default notice before we're done.

F

messages.subject: Re: counterparty — FM review / desk query
messages.body:

Advising the desk to document the missed deliveries but hold on any default notice until legal completes its assessment. We should have clarity in the next few days.

I'm relaying that to you on the basis of F's characterisation of the file, which is that the FM question is still open and that moving to a default notice now would be premature and risk a wrongful-termination exposure. Desk should treat the missed deliveries as failures under a suspended obligation for the time being, not as breaches under an active contract. Please pass that along to Louise's group.

G
